Fire on the base!|Moden Canady during the siege of D'Qar|}} '''Moden Canady''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served as a [[Navy|naval]] [[officer]] in both the [[Galactic Empire]] and the [[First Order]]. During the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the Empire, Canady commanded the [[Star Destroyer]] ''[[Solicitude]]'' of the [[Imperial Navy|Imperial Starfleet]]. He later joined the First Order, becoming [[captain]] of the [[Mandator IV-class Siege Dreadnought|Siege Dreadnought]] ''[[Fulminatrix]]'', a capacity in which he served during the [[Battle of D'Qar|evacuation of D'Qar]]. To his irritation, however, he had to put up with the crew of the ''Fulminatrix'', who were younger than him and, in Canady's view, inexperienced and arrogant. Canady, along with everyone else on his [[Starship|ship]], were [[Death|killed]] in a [[Resistance]] bombing run led by [[Poe Dameron]] in the [[Realspace|space]] battle above [[D'Qar]]. ==Biography== {{Quote|Captain Canady, why aren't you blasting that puny ship?"
"That puny ship is too small and at too close range. We need to scramble our fighters, five bloody minutes ago.|Armitage Hux and Moden Canady, speaking of Poe Dameron's X-wing|}} [[Reproduction|Born]] between [[25 BBY|25]] and [[16 BBY]], Moden Canady served as the [[commander]] of the [[Star Destroyer]] ''[[Solicitude]]'' of the [[Imperial Navy|Imperial Starfleet]] during the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. Following the Empire's [[Battle of Jakku|fall]], Canady became an [[First Order officer|officer]] of the [[First Order]]. He eventually became the [[captain]] of the ''[[Fulminatrix]]''. During the [[Battle of D'Qar|evacuation of D'Qar]], [[General]] [[Armitage Hux]] ordered Canady to command the ''Fulminatrix'' against the Resistance. During the battle, he ordered his warrant officer, [[Suday Bascus]], to reorient the ship's topside cannons and prepare the onboard fighter squadrons for deployment against the Resistance Fleet, and proceeded to sternly remind the man that there was a difference between the orders "prep for launch" and "launch" when Bascus protested that Hux had previously ordered for the ship not to deploy their fighter squadrons due to wanting to give a demonstration to the Resistance.''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition]]'' [[File:HuxHoloCanady-TheLastJedi1.jpg|thumb|202px|left|Canady speaking with Hux.]] In a surprise maneuver, [[Wing Commander]] [[Poe Dameron]] led a lone spearhead attack on the point-defense [[cannon]]s of the ''Fulminatrix'', to the annoyance of General Hux who demanded to know why Canady was not blasting the ship. Canady responded by stating that the ship was too fast and too close for the cannons and ordered his crew to launch their fighters. Canady was then informed by Bascus that there were several Resistance bombers approaching the dreadnought. While his fighters wiped out all but [[Cobalt Hammer|one]] of the bombers, Canady ordered the crew to fire on the [[Resistance base]], destroying the complex after it was fully evacuated and then had them target the main Resistance cruiser. Before they could fire, however, the [[gunner]] [[Paige Tico]] managed to launch her ship's payload of [[bomb]]s against the ''Fulminatrix'', causing systematic destruction. Accepting he had been bested, Canady stood firm silently respecting the courage of his enemies as his ship blew up, killing him and his loathed crew. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|What a bloody idiot.|Moden Canady, on Armitage Hux|[[The Last Jedi Adaptation 1|''The Last Jedi Adaptation'' 1]]}} [[File:CanadyOpinion-TheLastJedi1.jpg|thumb|right|261px|Canady gives his opinion of General Hux.]] A veteran [[Imperial officer|officer]] of the Galactic Empire, Moden Canady was proud to serve the First Order, just like when he served the Empire at the beginning of his career. However, he loathed having to serve alongside arrogant and inexperienced young First Order [[officer]]s due to their lack of discipline and failure to work as a team hindering his operational duties, to the point that he once entertained a brief fantasy of ejecting one out of an airlock. Despite this loathing, he nonetheless sympathized to a degree with their zeal for the First Order. Canady also detested serving under the command of General Armitage Hux, a First Order officer younger than him. He also held some irritation towards Hux, to the extent that he once denounced Hux as a "bloody idiot" after signing off, due to Hux insisting on continuing bad strategy. As Canady suspected, Hux's orders would prove to be his undoing, as Poe Dameron's and Paige Tico's actions eventually led to his own death. Unlike many officers of the First Order, however, Canady was honorable and he demonstrated that trait until the very end. When he became aware that the ''Fulminatrix'' had been defeated and there was no escape, he accepted his fate and remained on his [[Mandator IV-class Siege Dreadnought|''Mandator'' IV-class Siege Dreadnought]] rather than trying to flee. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|This actor is Mark Lewis Jones, who plays Canady. And God, I love him. He's just got such a powerful, "Fire on the base!". Matt Wood, who is our sound supervisor, was convinced that that line, "Fire on the base!", was going to start being used by EDM DJs. He might be right.|Director [[Rian Johnson]], in the audio commentary for ''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi''|{{Film|VIII}} Blu-ray Audio Commentary}} Canady was portrayed by [[Mark Lewis Jones]] in the [[2017]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']], the second installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[sequel trilogy]]. His surname was revealed in the film's credits, while his forename was first revealed in the accompanying reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: The Visual Dictionary]]'', which was written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]]. Mark Lewis Jones originally auditioned for a role in the [[2015]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']], but got no part on it, yet it's possible his name was kept on a list as he later received a call for ''The Last Jedi''.{{WebCite|url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/whats-on/film-news/star-wars-fans-watching-last-14046003|text=Star Wars fans watching The Last Jedi might recognise a familiar Welsh face in the opening scenes|date=2017-12-16|work=[[Wikipedia:Media Wales#WalesOnline|WalesOnline]]|archivedate=20200623111849}} Jones had previously provided the voice for [[Darth Decimus]] in the [[2011]] video game ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', which belongs to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity.''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' Canady's surname is a reference to May Dove Canady, the titular main character of the [[2002]] film [[Wikipedia:May (film)|''May'']], on which ''The Last Jedi'' director [[Rian Johnson]] previously worked as editor.{{Twitter|rianjohnson|status/946709577613144064|[[Rian Johnson]]|quote=I can neither confirm nor deny an- YES|archivefile=File:Rian_Johnson_Canady_tweet.png}}—[[Rian Johnson]] confirms that Moden Canady's name is a reference to ''May''.
